prohibited_claims: PostgreSQL is a second source of governed truth
Materialized views are live without explicit refresh proof
Schema-scoped dumps restore independently into a clean database without dependency proof
Backup/restore proves full product-state equivalence without digest comparison
Producer authority can be upgraded or flattened during materialization
Missing producer digest can be substituted with an unstable hash
PostgreSQL manages local installation or connection pooling

repository_estate.source_evidence_binding: SHA256 of T3.1 projection_digest. Refuses when producer digest is missing — no unstable Python hash() fallback.
repository_estate.authority_preservation: provenance_class, authority_state, corruption counts, and degradation metadata preserved as received from producer — no upgrading or flattening
repository_estate.rebuild_integrity: Deterministic rebuild via clear + re-materialize with schema-versioned, domain-bound canonical JSON digest manifests. Non-semantic columns (materialized_at, built_at, receipt_id) excluded by explicit justification.
repository_estate.corruption_degradation_state: Corrupt observations stored with provenance_class=corrupt_untrusted, authority_state=corrupt. Corruption events preserved from producer projection.
repository_estate.admission_for_x0: Allowed for operational rendering. X0 may display registered_repositories, repository_observations, workspace_instances, and observation_changes as derived operational projections. Must display provenance_class and authority_state labels. Must NOT display as canonical facts or live state.
prohibited: Display PostgreSQL rows as canonical repository facts
Display workspace paths (only salted root_path_digest is stored)
Claim real-time workspace state without explicit observation timestamp
Display raw repository hash as a navigable path

investigation_timeline.source_evidence_binding: SHA256 of timeline_id + canonical JSON of all projection rows. Determined at input construction time from the public projection contract.
investigation_timeline.authority_preservation: All 8 authority_classification values, 6 verification_class values, and degradation_detail text preserved from producer. Verified, corrupt, unverified, missing, and unsupported states remain distinguishable after PostgreSQL round-trip.
investigation_timeline.rebuild_integrity: Deterministic rebuild via delete + re-materialize with digest comparison. Schema-versioned manifests.
investigation_timeline.corruption_degradation_state: Degradation summary counts (verified_canonical, parsed_unverified, canonical_degraded, corrupt, unsupported, missing, contradictory, stale, canonical_live) preserved from T4.2 producer. Corrupt events stored with truthful degradation classification.
investigation_timeline.admission_for_x0: Allowed for operational rendering. X0 may display timeline events as derived operational projections grouped by authority classification. Must display authority_classification, verification_class, and degradation_detail. Canonical evidence classification labels must be preserved. Must NOT relabel derived timeline rows as canonical evidence.
prohibited: Relabel derived timeline rows as canonical evidence
Flatten authority_classification to a single trust label
Display timeline events without producer_digest_verified status
Claim timeline completeness without checking degradation_summary

publication_history.source_evidence_binding: SHA256 of canonical JSON encoding of every receipt's evidence_digest, compilation_successful, safety_passed, refusal_code, result_digest, and operation_id plus reconstruction corruption state. Changes in any receipt outcome with the same receipt_id produce a different digest. Unknown ledger identity is distinguishable from an empty or synthetic digest.
publication_history.authority_preservation: Compilation outcomes, safety results, refusal codes, deployment readiness, and preview-only flags preserved from T1.2 producer. Corruption state preserved in reconstruction. Ledger identity digest distinguishes known from unknown ledgers.
publication_history.rebuild_integrity: Deterministic rebuild via clear + re-materialize using source-evidence-bound input. Schema-versioned manifests.
publication_history.corruption_degradation_state: Corrupt rows preserved with reconstruction_warnings. Corrupt receipt rows refused during ledger load are counted but not stored (authoritative mode). Non-authoritative mode stores corrupt_rows count and corrupt_lines for visibility.
publication_history.admission_for_x0: Allowed for operational rendering. X0 may display publication_preview_receipts, reconstruction state, and build receipts as derived operational projections. Must display compilation_successful, safety_passed, refusal_code, and corruption_detected labels. Must NOT claim deployment readiness (always false for preview-only).
prohibited: Display deployment_ready as true (always false for preview-only evidence)
Claim publication receipts are canonical deployment records
Display raw receipt payloads or evidence_digest values
Bypass corruption_detected flag when displaying reconstruction state

backup_restore_equivalence.description: Restore verifies _schema_version and _migrations tables exist post-restore. Domain table content equivalence is proven by comparing pre-backup and post-restore domain digests (computed via compute_projection_digest). Full product-state equivalence requires additional digest comparison proof which is implemented but not yet verified to a clean-target database restore.

materialized_view_freshness.description: Materialized views are NOT auto-refreshed. They reflect the snapshot at the last explicit REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW call. X0 must NOT treat materialized view data as live or fresh. Concurrent refresh (REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY) requires a unique index on each view; this is not yet proven or offered. X0 may query base tables directly instead.
